chunks: God does not wrong the equal of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.

key_terms.مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ: the weight of a tiny seed or atom, denoting the smallest measure

ai.seo_question: How does God ensure justice and reward for even the smallest good deeds?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah An-Nisa is often cited to demonstrate the perfection of divine justice (Adl), where 'not wronging the weight of an atom' refers to the precise accounting of even minor deeds. The promise of multiplying good deeds and granting extra reward (Fadl) from Allah's own presence underscores the balance between justice and divine generosity, a key theme in Twelver theology regarding the Hereafter.
